albums.title: The Dark Side of the Moon
albums.reason: With 1199 all-time plays, Pink Floyd is one of your most beloved artists — this cornerstone album is the kind of thing that rewards a full, uninterrupted listen you probably haven't given it in years.

albums.title: Orbital (The Blue Album)
albums.reason: You've clocked 777 plays on Orbital and clearly love their work — the debut Blue Album is their rawest, most euphoric statement and a perfect deep-vault rediscovery alongside the Brown Album you've already revisited.

albums.title: First Impressions of Earth
albums.reason: Your 660 all-time Strokes plays and recent Room on Fire spin signal real love for the band — this underrated third album is rawer and stranger than their debut and ripe for a fresh listen.

albums.title: 100th Window
albums.reason: With 535 all-time plays on Massive Attack and Blue Lines, Mezzanine and Protection already revisited, this brooding, overlooked album in their catalogue is exactly the deep-vault corner you haven't visited recently.

albums.title: Dig Your Own Hole
albums.reason: You love The Chemical Brothers at 556 all-time plays — this is their peak statement, a wall-to-wall big-beat masterpiece that sits in a different era to Exit Planet Dust and deserves another full spin.

albums.title: Selected Ambient Works Volume II
albums.reason: Your 523 all-time plays on Aphex Twin and love of Xtal point straight here — this hushed, formless ambient classic is one of the most atmospheric records ever made and a world away from his faster work.

albums.title: Melt
albums.reason: Moderat appear heavily in your all-time plays and your recent track history includes Rusty Nails and Eating Hooks — Melt from their final album III is their most emotionally exposed and devastating single track, ripe for a focused revisit.

albums.title: Late Night Tales: Trentemøller
albums.reason: With 561 all-time plays and multiple Trentemøller albums in your history, this Late Night Tales mix captures his curatorial sensibility at its most intimate — a perfect late-evening listen you may not have returned to recently.

albums.title: Singularity
albums.reason: You clearly love Jon Hopkins — Open Eye Signal, Immunity and Collider are all in your history — and Singularity is the logical next step, a deeply immersive progression that belongs firmly in your recent vault.

albums.title: Animal Magic
albums.reason: You've explored Bonobo extensively across all eras and have 464 all-time plays — his debut is the one corner of the catalogue you've likely not revisited in a decade, raw and sample-heavy in the best way.

albums.title: Everything Ecstatic
albums.reason: Four Tet appeared in your 12-month listening and you have deep history with Rounds and other albums — Everything Ecstatic is his most kinetic and physically driven record, sitting in a sweet spot of the mid-2000s.

albums.title: Swim
albums.reason: Sun appears in your previously liked tracks and Caribou clearly resonates with you — Swim is his most cohesive and hypnotic album, a swirling psychedelic dance record that sits perfectly in your recent-vault era.

albums.title: Balance 019
albums.reason: Your all-time love of Air, Röyksopp and Massive Attack points toward this Viennese producer's luxurious cinematic trip-hop — Waldeck blends orchestral strings, jazz and electronic texture in a way that fits your taste perfectly.

albums.title: Great Lengths
albums.reason: Your deep love of Burial, Kode9 adjacents and Underworld's murky electronic side makes Martyn's debut a natural discovery — it fuses dubstep space, jungle rhythms and deep house warmth into something genuinely singular.

albums.title: Two/Three
albums.reason: Your all-time love of Kanye, Modeselektor and Flying Lotus-adjacent sounds points to Dabrye's cult Detroit hip-hop/electronic crossover — sharp, rhythmically inventive and strangely overlooked for how good it is.

albums.title: Machines Learning
albums.reason: Your 1017 plays of Leftfield and love of hard, rhythmically dense electronic music like Modeselektor and Justice lead naturally to SCNTST's precision-engineered, dystopian machine-funk — a cult record that deserves far more attention.

albums.title: Hinterland
albums.reason: Your love of Trentemøller, Plaid and Max Cooper's textural depth points to Recondite — this is minimal techno at its most emotionally resonant, slow-burning and atmospheric in exactly the way you tend to love.

albums.title: Silhouette Brown
albums.reason: Your all-time love of Massive Attack, The Avalanches and Stevie Wonder creates a perfect entry point for this obscure UK duo who fused neo-soul, trip-hop and jazz into one of the most underheard albums of the 2000s.

albums.title: Phases
albums.reason: Your 12-month arc through Sault, Charles Bradley and Alabaster Deplume shows a clear hunger for soulful music with political depth and personality — Moonchild Sanelly's South African afro-house-soul fusion is the boldest step in that direction.

albums.title: Float
albums.reason: Your recent deep immersion in Nils Frahm, Hania Rani, Joep Beving and Ben Lukas Boysen points unmistakably to Peter Broderick's quiet, violin-and-piano debut — intimate, human and emotionally devastating in the best way.

albums.title: Prender el Alma
albums.reason: Your current listening through Hermanos Gutiérrez, O'Flynn and Viken Arman signals a love of music rooted in non-Western tradition filtered through modern electronics — Nicola Cruz's debut is exactly that, a stunning Ecuadorian-electronic crossover.

albums.title: Black Classical Music
albums.reason: Your recent engagement with Portico Quartet, Oscar Peterson Trio and Khruangbin shows an appetite for rhythmically inventive, groove-led jazz — Yussef Dayes' solo debut is the most exciting thing to happen in that space in years.

albums.title: Knock Knock
albums.reason: Your recent Folamour, O'Flynn and Axel Boman listening traces a clear line through warm, witty and emotionally unpredictable house music — DJ Koze's Knock Knock is the masterclass in that world, lush and deeply strange.

albums.title: Brute
albums.reason: Your arc through Apparat, Max Cooper and Brambles' ambient weight points toward Fatima Al Qadiri's dense, politically charged electronic work — Brute is concise, urgent and unlike almost anything else you've been listening to.

albums.title: Solan Goose
albums.reason: You played Erland Cooper this month and your recent listening through Ólafur Arnalds and Nils Frahm shows a clear current pull toward emotionally spacious, nature-rooted music — Solan Goose is his finest, most atmospheric work.

albums.title: The Mute Monk
albums.reason: Stavroz appeared in your listening this month and their blend of live percussion, folk instruments and deep house groove is clearly where you are right now — The Mute Monk is their most fully realised collection.

albums.title: Siku
albums.reason: Nicola Cruz featured in your last-month plays and this follow-up to his debut goes deeper and stranger — if the first album drew you in, Siku will reward the deeper dive you're clearly ready for right now.

albums.title: Branches
albums.reason: Viken Arman appeared in your most recent listening and Belong was clearly resonating — Branches is his debut album and gathers that same spiritual, piano-rooted organic house into a cohesive and deeply moving full listen.

albums.title: The Journey of a Shaman Prince to the Kingdom of Fools
albums.reason: Folamour is active in both your monthly and 12-month listening right now — this album captures his most playful and emotionally generous side, sitting perfectly alongside the warm, groove-led music you've been reaching for lately.

albums.title: Xique-Xique
albums.reason: Xique-Xique appeared in your plays this month and their self-titled album is the ideal companion — hypnotic, percussion-driven Brazilian music that shares the ritualistic organic energy of everything else you're gravitating toward right now.

songs.title: Kashmir
songs.reason: You've racked up 965 plays on Led Zeppelin and this is arguably their greatest single piece of music — a monumental, hypnotic slab of rock that probably hasn't had a proper listen from you in years.

songs.title: A Cowboy Appropriate for the Times
songs.reason: You love The Avalanches at 531 all-time plays and Since I Left You is a touchstone — this deep cut from that album is a joyful, densely layered collage gem that rewards the kind of nostalgic rediscovery this tier is built for.

songs.title: Red Alert
songs.reason: Your 496 plays on Basement Jaxx and love of Raindrops shows real affection — Red Alert from Remedy is their most emotionally charged floor-filler, an ecstatic piece of late-90s dance music ripe for a nostalgic blast.

songs.title: Honey
songs.reason: With 551 all-time Moby plays and Play as a touchstone, Honey is the deep-vault track worth revisiting — built on a raw gospel sample, it's one of the most emotionally direct things he ever made and hugely nostalgic.

songs.title: Caring Is Creepy
songs.reason: You love The Shins at 546 all-time plays and New Slang is already in your history — Caring Is Creepy is the other great track from Oh, Inverted World, their most lo-fi and emotionally raw early gem.

songs.title: Feel Good Inc.
songs.reason: Gorillaz sit at 364 all-time plays for you, and Demon Days is one of the defining albums of the mid-2000s — Feel Good Inc. is the perfect nostalgic reentry point, enormous and strangely melancholic at the same time.

songs.title: Vale
songs.reason: Maribou State are deep in your all-time history and you've explored Hallowed extensively — Vale from that album is a standout track you may not have singled out recently, lush and emotionally expansive in their signature way.

songs.title: Re
songs.reason: You have 67 plays on Nils Frahm in the last 12 months and All Melody is well-loved — Re from Solo is one of his most quietly devastating pieces, a slow-building piano meditation perfect for where your taste has been heading.

songs.title: Glue
songs.reason: Bicep appeared in your recent listening and your history shows a deep love of emotional dance music — Glue is one of the most beloved house tracks of the last decade, a pure nostalgic rush that earns its recent-vault place.

songs.title: Never Catch Me (feat. Kendrick Lamar)
songs.reason: Flying Lotus is in your history with Los Angeles already explored — Never Catch Me from You're Dead! is the track where his jazz-electronic vision hit its absolute peak, and it's the ideal recent-vault rediscovery.

songs.title: Rough Sleeper
songs.reason: Burial's Archangel and Shell of Light are both in your history, placing him firmly in your recent vault — Rough Sleeper is one of his most ambitious and emotionally exhausting long tracks, well worth returning to in full.

songs.title: Particles
songs.reason: You have 27 plays on Ólafur Arnalds in the last 12 months and his sound is clearly resonating with you right now — Particles from Re:member is one of his most melodically radiant and emotionally open moments, distinct from Near Light and worth its own revisit.

songs.title: Loops from the Bergain
songs.reason: Your all-time love of Leftfield, Underworld and Orbital's minimal-to-peak electronic arcs points directly to Swayzak — this track is a quietly legendary piece of Berlin-influenced minimal techno that flew totally under the radar.

songs.title: So Many Dreams
songs.reason: Your all-time love of Stevie Wonder, Marvin Gaye and Bonobo's jazz-soul crossover creates a perfect entry to Dego's broken-beat soul — a veteran UK producer making music of extraordinary emotional depth that most people have missed.

songs.title: Devotion
songs.reason: Your all-time love of James Blake's fractured emotional electronics and Burial's atmospheric murk make Tirzah an obvious fit — Devotion is a hushed, deeply intimate UK electronic pop record that shares that same bruised, minimal DNA.

songs.title: Wraether
songs.reason: Your 1017 plays on Leftfield and love of Trentemøller's dark melodic techno draws a clear line to Alex Smoke — this Scottish producer's debut is packed with moody, melodic techno that sits in a totally underexplored corner of your taste.

songs.title: Fabric 50
songs.reason: Your all-time love of deep house adjacents — Basement Jaxx, Faithless, Orbital at their most subtle — leads naturally to Move D, one of the great unsung architects of deep house, and this Fabric mix is the perfect introduction.

songs.title: What Does Your Soul Look Like (Part 1 - Blue Sky Revisit)
songs.reason: Your all-time love of The Avalanches' sample wizardry and Moby's emotionally direct sampling points to this DJ Shadow deep cut — a slow, beatless ambient-sample piece that shows a completely different side of one of the great producers.

songs.title: Truth
songs.reason: Your 12-month arc through Oscar Peterson Trio, Portico Quartet and Nduduzo Makhathini-adjacent jazz sounds has been building toward the grandeur of Kamasi Washington — Truth from The Epic is his most emotionally overwhelming moment.

songs.title: Innerspace
songs.reason: Your recent listening through Portico Quartet, Four Tet and O'Flynn's ambient-dance crossover points directly to Rejoicer's quietly brilliant Tel Aviv jazz-electronic fusion — Innerspace is intimate, groove-led and deeply soulful.

songs.title: Now
songs.reason: Your 12-month engagement with Sault, Charles Bradley and Alabaster Deplume's spiritual-political soul points here — this Chicago ensemble makes music of radical collective joy, and Now is one of the most joyful and urgent records in years.

songs.title: Still Life
songs.reason: Your consistent return to Nils Frahm, Ben Lukas Boysen and Hania Rani over the last 12 months shows a real home in Nordic minimalist piano music — Jonatan Backelie's Still Life is a hidden gem directly in that lineage.

songs.title: Lonely Planet
songs.reason: Your current listening through O'Flynn, Folamour and Axel Boman traces a clear love of warm, sun-drenched and cosmically minded house music — Tornado Wallace's debut is a masterwork of that exact Balearic-electronic feeling.

songs.title: Find Me in the Dark (feat. Virginia)
songs.reason: Your current pull toward Stavroz, Viken Arman and the more ritualistic end of your recent listening opens a door to Lena Willikens — this track is hypnotic, strange and emotionally raw in a way that fits exactly where you are now.

songs.title: If You Want to Be Free
songs.reason: Crazy P are your most-played artist this month and you've been deep in their catalogue — If You Want to Be Free is a soaring, emotionally generous disco-house anthem from their back catalogue worth spotlighting right now.

songs.title: Sule Skerry
songs.reason: You played Erland Cooper this month and your Solan Goose album recommendation fits this current mood perfectly — Sule Skerry is the album's most haunting individual track, all wind-swept strings and field recording depth.

songs.title: Fearless
songs.reason: Folamour is active in your listening right now and Fearless has already been a standout track in your 12-month history — it captures exactly the ecstatic, emotionally generous house energy you're clearly craving this week.

songs.title: The Mute Monk
songs.reason: Stavroz appeared in your most recent listening and their sound — organic instruments, ritualistic percussion, deep groove — is clearly resonating with where you are right now; this track is their most hypnotic centrepiece.

songs.title: Puente
songs.reason: Nicola Cruz is in your recent month plays and Puente from his debut is the track that best captures his vision — a deep, bass-heavy piece that fuses Andean tradition with modern club music energy perfectly suited to your current mood.

songs.title: Wind Chimes
songs.reason: Viken Arman appeared in your most recent plays and Belong clearly moved you — Wind Chimes is the most intimate and quietly devastating track on Branches, a perfect companion to the reflective, spiritual mood you're carrying right now.
